question: The Eld's deer subspecies, which is classified as endangered in the IUCN Red List, is found only in the:

options.text: Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur
Pench National Park in Madhya Pradesh

solution:
The correct answer is __**Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**__**Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur**__

__
 
• The only** floating National Park in the world**.
 
• Located on **Loktak Lake is the last natural habitat of the 'Sangai'** (Eld's deer), the **dancing deer of Manipur**.
 
• A glimpse of the deer in this unique wetland ecosystem is a must for any wildlife enthusiast.

 IUCN Red List

 
• The International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List of Threatened Species.
 
• Also known as the Red Data Book, founded in 1964.
 
• It is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of biological species.
 
• Animals, plant and fungi species, subspecies, varieties and subpopulations can be assessed on the Red List.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Hemis National Park in Ladakh**

 
• Globally famous for its **snow leopards (**believed to have the **highest density of them in any protected area in the world).**
 
• The **Tibetan wolf, the Eurasian brown bear (endangered in India), and the red fox** are also present in Hemis.

**Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan**

 
• Known for its **large tiger population**.
 
• There has been a** decline in the tiger population in Ranthambhore due to poaching and other reasons.**

**Pench National Park in Madhya Pradesh**

 
• This park is **home to a number of endangered species**.
 
• There are **25 tigers, 3 species of amphibians, 39 species of mammals, 13 species of reptiles and 285 species of birds.**
 
• **Indian leopard, sloth bear, Indian wolf, wild dog, porcupine, monkeys, jungle cat, fox, striped hyena, gaur, four-horned antelope and barking deer** are protected.
